proposed.explanation:
You already hold 400 shares of ABUK (Abu Qir Fertilizers), valued at 30,484 EGP, alongside 20,000 EGP in cash, for a total portfolio of 50,484 EGP. Your stated goal is to keep a fertilizer exporter as a currency hedge over a 5-year horizon, and ABUK fits that role. The verified evidence from the 9-month 2026 results shows basic EPS of 8.74 EGP for the nine months ended 30 Sep 2026, up from 4.28 EGP in the same period a year earlier — a roughly 104% year-on-year increase computed from the two verified per-share figures. This strong earnings momentum supports the investment thesis for a fertilizer exporter whose revenues are denominated in foreign currency, which is the hedge you are seeking.

I recommend holding your existing 400 shares rather than buying or selling. A buy is not advisable here: ABUK already represents about 60% of your total portfolio value, and the diversification rule caps any single holding at 50% after a purchase, so no additional shares can be added without breaching that limit. A sell would contradict your stated 5-year currency-hedge objective, and the earnings trend does not signal deterioration.

Important caveats and uncertainties: (1) The evidence is limited to a single page of the 9-month results; I have no data on export volumes, contract pricing, foreign-currency mix, or forward guidance. (2) Several key figures on the same page — total net profit for both periods, the Q3-2026 EPS, and all percentage-change columns — are marked AMBIGUOUS due to OCR or unit-line conflicts (the page mixes 'billion' and 'million' labels). I could not verify the absolute profit levels or the exact quarterly 2026 EPS, so my read of the earnings picture rests solely on the two verified 9-month EPS figures and the one verified Q3-2025 EPS. (3) Fertilizer prices are cyclical and sensitive to global demand, energy costs, and trade policy; a 5-year horizon helps smooth cycles but does not eliminate drawdown risk. (4) With medium loss tolerance and a separate emergency fund, your liquidity position is adequate, but you should monitor ABUK's export earnings and EGP/USD dynamics at least semi-annually. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.
